args.summary: AC-story: Search results page has insufficient color contrast on "Only 1 left" product badge (WCAG AA 1.4.3)
args.description:
**Failure type: assertion failure on a reachable page — the application was reached, the search results loaded, and the axe-core scan reported a WCAG violation.**

**Steps to reproduce (from the automated test):**
1. Navigate to `/#/search?q=Juice`
2. Wait for the search results to load in the `main` content area
3. Run an axe-core WCAG 2.x A/AA scan scoped to the `main` element

**Expected:**
No WCAG A/AA violations — all text on the search results page meets minimum contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text per WCAG 1.4.3).

**Actual:**
axe-core reports a `color-contrast` (serious) violation on:
`app-product:nth-child(6) > mat-card > article > aside > span[translate=""]`
Measured contrast: 2.86:1; required: 4.5:1.

This is the "Only 1 left" availability badge displayed on a product card in the search results. The text colour against its background does not meet the minimum contrast ratio required by WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (Level AA).

**What was ruled out:**
- The scan was scoped to the `<main>` element to exclude the cookie consent banner, welcome dialog, header and any other site-wide widgets unrelated to this story's behaviour. The violation is within the search results product list — it is not a false positive from a peripheral widget.
- The test was run twice (unchanged between runs, ledger entries 153 and 166) and produced the same violation both times, ruling out a transient or environmental failure.
- The test logic and assertion are correct: `expect(violations.map(v => v.id).sort()).toEqual([])` — any violation causes the test to fail with the violation IDs, which is what happened here.

**Confidence: High** — the preconditions held (page loaded, results rendered, scan scoped correctly), and the same violation reproduced on two consecutive runs.
